source: AI Video Bootcamp's Color Grading Reference (Mood -> Color -> Prompt cheat sheet) and its Film Look References section - the prompt words and palette descriptions are the course's own, not invented.
note: A mood or a film look is a single named recipe (mutually exclusive with each other - two complete looks can't both be the grade), or type your own. `techniques` stack on top of either, additive and opt-in. Unlike lighting's quality x source, there's nothing here to contradict itself, so no conflicts list. Some of this material is deliberately vivid rather than restrained (neon cyberpunk, hot pink Barbie) - every phrase is checked against banned/warn, not just detectability, since this is the first bank whose source leans stylised.

epic-heroic.label: Epic / Heroic
epic-heroic.phrase: warm golden highlights, deep blue shadows, rich cinematic color grading, epic tone
epic-heroic.note: Rich golds, deep blues, warm highlights with cool shadows.

dark-moody.label: Dark / Moody
dark-moody.phrase: dark moody color grading, desaturated tones, deep shadows, teal and orange palette
dark-moody.note: Desaturated, heavy shadows, teal and orange undertones.

romantic-dreamy.label: Romantic / Dreamy
romantic-dreamy.phrase: soft dreamy color grading, warm pink and gold tones, gentle haze, romantic atmosphere
romantic-dreamy.note: Soft pinks, warm golden tones, slight haze.

mad-max-fury-road.note: Crushed teal shadows with blazing orange/amber highlights, extreme contrast.

accent-echo.label: Accent colour echo
accent-echo.phrase: one accent colour repeated through the frame, in a reflection or object
accent-echo.note: Repeating a single accent colour makes the frame feel intentional, like every element belongs, rather than random.

warm-cool-contrast.label: Warm/cool contrast
warm-cool-contrast.phrase: warm light on the subject against cooler tones in the background, the classic complementary colour contrast
warm-cool-contrast.note: Orange and blue sit opposite each other on the colour wheel - warm skin against a cool background is one of the strongest, most reliable colour separations there is.
